title: Transformers and turns ratio
idea: Voltage follows the turns, current goes the opposite way, and impedance follows the square of the turns ratio.

core.text: V out = V in x N out / N in
lines: Current goes the other way: more volts out means less current out
So to match impedances: turns ratio = √(impedance ratio)
Works by mutual inductance: the primary's field links the secondary

compare.how: More turns on the output. Voltage up, current down, so the input winding needs thicker wire.
Fewer turns on the output. Voltage down, current up. Feed it backward and it steps up.

traps.why: That divides by 3. The secondary has more turns, so voltage goes up: 120 x 3 = 360 V.
12 is the impedance ratio (600 / 50). The turns ratio is its square root, about 3.5.

traps.wrong: The input voltage is divided by 4
traps.why: That's the normal direction. Fed from the secondary, a 4:1 step-down steps up by 4.

traps.wrong: To improve the coupling between the primary and secondary
traps.why: Wire size is about current. A step-up's primary carries more current than its secondary.
The windings share a magnetic field, not an electric one: mutual inductance.
